keyword: how to become an app developer after 10th
title: How to Become an App Developer After 10th (2026)
desc: An honest plan to become an app developer after Class 10: web and full-stack app skills, where native Android and iOS fit in, projects and salary.
h1: How to become an app developer after 10th
an honest roadmap for web, cloud and mobile apps
lead: A plan for a Class 10 student and their parent to read together. It uses a real 624-hour, three-year software curriculum and is clear about one thing: it builds web and full-stack apps, and native phone apps are an extra step.
role_intro: An app developer builds applications people use to get something done: booking a ticket, tracking homework, paying a bill. Some apps run in a browser, some are installed from the Play Store or App Store, and almost all of them talk to a backend and a database in the cloud.

day_to_day.answer: An app developer spends the day building screens and user flows, connecting them to APIs and databases, handling logins and saved data, and testing that the whole task works from the first tap to the last.
day_to_day.html:
Work usually starts from a user task, such as booking a slot or tracking homework. You build the screens for each step and decide what the app remembers between visits. You call the backend to load and save data, and handle logins. Then you test the full flow, including what happens with no internet or a wrong password. You work with designers, backend developers and testers.

In this roadmap, JavaScript, React and TypeScript build the screens. APIs, SQL and NoSQL databases handle data, and AWS runs the backend. Installable phone apps need other tools, such as Android Studio with Kotlin, which this program does not teach.

How it differs from a web developer. A web developer focuses on pages that open in a browser and look right everywhere. An app developer focuses on a task across many screens: state, saved data, logins, and often more than one platform. A responsive web app opens on a phone, but it is not the same as a Play Store or App Store app.

first_project.answer: A realistic first project is a homework planner that runs in the browser: add a task, mark it done and keep it after a refresh, built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript in about two to three weeks.
first_project.html:
Week 1: draw the screens on paper: the task list, the add form and the done view. Build them in HTML and CSS so they fit a phone screen. Week 2: use JavaScript to add, tick and delete tasks, then save them in the browser's local storage so they survive a refresh. Week 3: add a due date and sort by it, then ask a friend to use it on their phone and fix what confused them. It runs in a phone's browser. It is not an installable app.

This leads to the JavaScript Interactive App and the API-Driven Web Application in year 1 of the program. If you also want to try a real Android app, Google's Android Basics with Compose is a separate course outside this program.

in_short: An app developer builds around a task a user wants done, such as booking or tracking, across screens, saved data, logins and the backend.
This roadmap builds web and full-stack apps with React, TypeScript, APIs and the cloud. It has no native Android or iOS module.
Phone apps are an extra step on top. Take a separate Android or iOS course once your logic and backend base is strong.
start_answer: Yes, but plan in two parts: after Class 10 you can build browser-based and full-stack apps through this roadmap, then add native Android or iOS skills separately, because this program does not teach them.

start_extra: Many students say app developer when they mean phone apps. That is a fine goal, but the screen is only one part. The logic, data and cloud skills behind an app take the longest to learn, and they are the same for web and mobile.
roadmap_answer: The roadmap runs in three years: year 1 builds programming logic and interactive web apps, year 2 adds APIs, databases, security and cloud deployment, and year 3 builds cloud-native, full-stack applications; native Android or iOS is learned separately on top.
year_focus: Year 1: programming logic, Java and your first interactive web apps
Year 2: the backend, data and cloud services every app depends on
Year 3: cloud-native applications and a product-ready portfolio
fit_note: Be clear about the fit. The Software Development program builds web and full-stack applications with React, APIs, databases and the cloud. It has no dedicated native Android or iOS module, so it does not teach Kotlin, Swift, Play Store or App Store publishing. If phone apps are your goal, plan to learn a native platform on top, for example through the Android Basics with Compose course from Android Developers. For an earlier, lighter start, see AI Foundation.
skills_answer: An app developer needs programming logic, an object-oriented language, a front-end framework, API and backend skills, databases, security and cloud deployment, plus, for phone apps, a native platform such as Android with Kotlin, which this roadmap does not cover.

certs_answer: The roadmap prepares for front-end and cloud developer certificates, which suit the backend and web side of apps; it does not prepare for any Android or iOS certificate, and each certificate is awarded by its own provider.

cert_notes.Meta Front-End Developer Professional Ce: A beginner-level, 9-course series on Coursera covering HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React, with a capstone where you build your own front-end web application.
cert_notes.AWS Certified Developer – Associate: Validates developing, testing, deploying and debugging cloud-based applications on AWS. AWS recommends one or more years of hands-on experience first.

cert_extra: For Android, Google's Android Basics with Compose is a self-paced online course that teaches Kotlin and Jetpack Compose over 8 units. Its listed prerequisites are basic computer skills, basic maths skills and a computer that can run Android Studio. It is separate from this program.
notfor_answer: This program is not the right fit if you only want to build native Android or iOS apps from day one, want a guaranteed job, or are not willing to add a mobile platform through extra study later.

salary_answer: Indicative ranges for software and application development roles in India are about ₹4 to 8 lakh a year for freshers, ₹10 to 20 lakh at 3 to 5 years, and ₹25 to 50 lakh or more for senior developers.
faqs: How many years does it take to become an app developer after 10th?

Plan for about three years of steady work to build strong app foundations, such as this 624-hour roadmap, plus extra time if you want native Android or iOS skills on top. Many students also complete a degree.
Can I become an app developer without maths?

Yes, for most app building, which relies on logic more than advanced maths. Google's Android course lists basic maths skills as a prerequisite. A B.Tech through JEE Main still needs Physics and Mathematics in Class 12.
Will I learn Android or iOS app development in this program?
No. The program builds web and full-stack applications with React, APIs and the cloud. It has no dedicated native Android or iOS module, so those are learned separately on top.
Why not start directly with Android or iOS?
You can. But every app needs logic, data, APIs and a backend. This roadmap builds those first, and they stay useful whichever platform you choose later.
Can a React web app work on phones?
Yes, a responsive web app opens in a phone's browser. It is not the same as an installable Play Store or App Store app, which needs native or mobile framework skills.
context_fact: Nasscom's Strategic Review 2026 describes cloud-native architecture as widespread across India's $315 billion tech industry. Most apps, web or mobile, now depend on cloud services, which is why this roadmap spends time on the backend and the cloud.
